Reviewed: genuine homonym across eras. In Enlightenment/Revolutions, 'popular sovereignty' means legitimate authority derives from the consent of the governed. In Civil War, 'popular sovereignty' is the specific antebellum doctrine (Kansas-Nebraska Act) of letting a territory's settlers vote on whether to permit slavery. Two established, distinct historical meanings of the same term.
